title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Problem (§43, case VI): find the transverse vibrations of an elastic rod whose two ends are both clamped. This is the clamped–clamped beam.

Setup from the earlier sections. The mode shape is y = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f). Separation of the beam equation gives a time factor sin(ζ + ω²c√(2gb) t/a²), with ω = a/f.

Clamped end s = 0 (y = 0, y' = 0):
- α + β + δ = 0 and α − β + γ = 0.
- Hence δ = −α − β and γ = −α + β.

Clamped end s = a (ω = a/f):
- α e^ω + β e^{−ω} + γ sin ω + δ cos ω = 0.
- α e^ω − β e^{−ω} + γ cos ω − δ sin ω = 0.

Substitution gives two linear equations in α, β:
- α(e^ω − sin ω − cos ω) + β(e^{−ω} + sin ω − cos ω) = 0.
- α(e^ω − cos ω + sin ω) − β(e^{−ω} − cos ω − sin ω) = 0.

Each yields a value of α/β. Equating the two (vanishing determinant) gives cos ω · (e^ω + e^{−ω})/2 = 1, i.e. cos ω cosh ω = 1. Euler remarks this is exactly the frequency equation of case I (free–free rod). So the clamped–clamped rod has the same spectrum, with ω ≈ 3π/2, 5π/2, 7π/2, … and frequencies ∝ ω²: 9, 25, 49, 81, … times π²c√(2gb)/(4a²).

Mode shape:
- Using cos ω = sech ω, Euler takes sin ω = ±tanh ω (sign = sign of sin ω).
- This gives α = 1, β = ∓e^ω, γ = −(1 ± e^ω), δ = −(1 ∓ e^ω).
- So the mode differs from the free–free mode only in the signs of γ and δ.
- The next page assembles the general motion as a superposition of such modes and shows that the shapes differ greatly from the free–free case although the tones coincide.
errors: The listed sounds are printed as 9πc√(2gb)/(4aa), 25πc√(2gb)/(4aa), etc. Since the frequency factor is ω²c√(2gb)/a² with ω = (2n+1)π/2, they should contain π² (9ππ…, 25ππ…). This is a misprint, or an inherited slip from case I.

The roots ω = 3π/2, 5π/2, … are only approximations, adequate because sech ω is tiny. The true roots of cos ω cosh ω = 1 are 4.7300, 7.8532, 10.9956, …; the first exceeds 3π/2 = 4.7124 by about 0.4%. The text states them as if exact ('iidem erunt').
Minor: the two substituted equations are printed without '= 0'.

Algebra otherwise checked: the substitutions, both α/β ratios, the reduction to cos ω = 2/(e^ω + e^{−ω}), and α = 1, β = ∓e^ω, γ = −(1 ± e^ω), δ = −(1 ∓ e^ω) are all correct (upper sign when sin ω > 0).

ideas.what: Frequency equation of the clamped–clamped beam, cos ω cosh ω = 1, with approximate roots (2n+1)π/2
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Bernoulli beam eigenvalue problem, clamped–clamped boundary conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E526, 1774/1782); Daniel Bernoulli for the related free–free and cantilever cases
ideas.where_published: E526 itself; discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11.2)

ideas.what: Observation that clamped–clamped and free–free rods are isospectral but have totally different mode shapes
ideas.modern_name: Free–free / clamped–clamped spectral coincidence (apart from rigid-body modes); boundary-condition duality of the beam operator
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; later restated by Rayleigh (Theory of Sound) and Strehlke
ideas.where_published: E526 §§43–44; also noted in Euler's other rod-vibration papers (e.g. E443/E444, unsure of exact one)

ideas.what: Closed-form normalisation of the mode coefficients using sin ω = ±tanh ω
ideas.modern_name: Mode shape of the clamped–clamped beam

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, well-documented part of Euler's classification of the six end-condition cases in E526, analysed in detail by Truesdell. The free–free / clamped–clamped coincidence is classical. The only issues are a misprint (π instead of π²) and approximate roots.
transcription_corrections: 'fin.' and 'cof.' should be read as 'ſin.' (sine) and 'coſ.' (cosine) throughout.
The two substituted equations ('α(e^ω − ſin.ω − coſ.ω) + β(…)' and 'α(e^ω − coſ.ω + ſin.ω) − β(…)') implicitly equal 0; '= o' is not printed.
The sounds read in the image as '9πc√2gb/4aa' etc. (single π), which is faithful to the print but mathematically should be π².
